# Roadmap

The public plan page: milestones, then epics, then issues, read from GitHub. No collection; the
page is static and refreshes itself. Routes: [screens](/docs/reference/routes.md).

## Screens

| Screen                 | Route                                        | Data comes from                                                            |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The plan               | `/roadmap`                                   | `getPlan` (GitHub milestones, epic issues and their sub-issues)            |
| One mission            | `/roadmap/missions/[number]`                 | the same plan, `getMission`; the number must be a milestone the plan lists |
| One issue              | `/roadmap/[number]`                          | the same plan, `getPlanIssue`; the number must be one the plan shows       |
| One issue, in a dialog | `/roadmap/[number]` from a click on the plan | the same page's content (`IssueDetail`), shown in a dialog over the plan   |

## Behaviors and events

- GitHub is the only source. The page reads milestones, issues labeled `epic` and each epic's sub-issues over GitHub's REST API (`data/github.ts`); nothing is copied into the CMS, so nothing can drift.
- The plan page's one heading is "What we’re building", in the shared page header at its usual size, with no small label above it (#1082, #1106).
- Both pages are static and re-render every hour (`revalidate = 3600`, `PLAN_REVALIDATE_SECONDS`). Both ask search engines not to index them.
- Screened out, and never shown or counted as shown: issues labeled `infra` or `needs owner`, and any issue whose title or text holds a server address, an email address or a plug-and-play plan. A screened epic takes its sub-issues with it. A milestone left with no shown epic is not listed at all, and comes back by itself when one of its epics can be shown (#1081). A milestone whose title or description fails the screen shows as "Milestone N" with no description. Label names are screened too, and the hidden labels match in any case. The screen is best effort: it finds IPv4 addresses and plain email addresses, not every spelling. The page says how many issues are not shown (`domain/screen.ts`, `domain/plan.ts`).
- Clicking an issue or epic on the plan opens it in a dialog over the plan, and its close button, back button, Escape and the browser's back button return to the plan where it was. A direct visit, a refresh or a shared link shows the issue's own page, so every address works without a script. The dialog and the page show the same `IssueDetail` (`app/(frontend)/roadmap/@modal`, `ui/IssueDetail.tsx`, #946). While the dialog is open the browser tab shows the issue's title, and the site's title returns when it closes; the dialog and the page get their title and "do not index" rule from one function, `planIssueMetadata` (#954).
- A state mark is green for open, purple for done and gray for not planned, each with its words and an icon, in a slightly bigger size than the plain-outline labels beside it, so the state stands out (`ui/IssueBadges.tsx`, #946, #952).
- A screened, unknown or malformed issue number answers 404, so a screened issue can't be reached by its address.
- The plan page lists the missions, freshest first. On a tablet they are blocks of one size (two across; three on a desktop); on a phone they are boxes that start closed (`ui/PlanTiles.tsx`, `ui/MissionBlock.tsx`, `ui/MissionAccordion.tsx`, #1193). Each shows the mission's name (a link to its page on a block, an "Open this mission" link inside a box), a small "3 of 5 done" and a dot: filled when something was finished in the last 7 days, hollow when it was quiet, with the same in words for screen readers (`ui/ActivityMark.tsx`). A block shows the week as a heat map as wide as the block; a box opens to that heat map and its projects, each of which opens to its own week and its issues. Projects not yet in a mission follow in their own group, then a small "Tell us" button for anything missing. The plan page no longer shows a mission's due date or description.
- The top of the page is three graphs over the last four weeks (finished per day, done in all, still open, each with one small figure: finished in the last 7 days, done in all, open now) and, under them, a four-week activity map of the days issues were finished, then the "Updated" line (`ui/PlanSummary.tsx`, #1192). The map is also the plan's day filter (next bullet). A phone stacks the graphs, a tablet puts finished on top and the other two side by side, a desktop puts all three in a row. Each graph and the map have a text equivalent listing every value. Progress counts open and done issues, and ones closed as not planned are left out. Days are counted in the site timezone (`domain/stats.ts`).
- **Month browsing** (#1218). The map starts on the last four weeks. Arrows above it step back one whole calendar month at a time (the previous month in full, then the one before, as far back as the first issue activity) and forward again until the four weeks return; the three graphs stay on four weeks. A past month shows no today ring and no dashed days to come. Days chosen stay chosen while browsing, and their pills keep their counts (`domain/mapWindow.ts`, `ui/DayFilterMap.client.tsx`).
- **Activity map caption** (#1205). The four-week map fills the width of the page like the graphs above it and has "Work done per day" under its squares at the left with a Less-to-More key at the right, on one line, and more space around it; the day pills sit below both.
- **Day filter** (#1204). Nothing is chosen when the page loads, so it, and the page without scripts, show the whole plan. Pressing a day on the four-week map shows only the issues opened or finished on it; the missions and projects stay as containers and a mission or project with no such issue is hidden. Each chosen day is a pill under the map with its day, a check and its finished count, and a dot and its opened count; pills stack and wrap, and a day comes out by pressing it again or pressing its pill. Several days mean any of them, and a line says how many issues show. A day with nothing shows "Nothing was opened or finished then" and a button back to the whole plan. A mission's week strip, and a project's inside a phone box, can narrow further. **The top commands the lower levels:** with nothing chosen above, any day of the strip can be picked; under a single day that day is fixed, ringed, and every other day is unavailable; under two or more days only those days can be pressed and every other day is a muted, slashed square that cannot be focused or pressed and is read out as "not available, not selected above". A level with no pick follows the level above, its counts count only the issues on the days that are on, and a pick on a day the level above removes drops out. A mission or project that holds a pick of its own stays on the page even when that day has nothing in it, with the day selected, so it can be pressed again; one with nothing only because of the days above is hidden. Only issues are filtered by day, and a filtered issue still opens in the dialog with its "See it on GitHub" link. The filter is a small client piece over the same static page (`domain/dayFilter.ts` and `domain/filterPlan.ts` hold the rules; `ui/PlanFilter.client.tsx`, `ui/DayFilterMap.client.tsx`, `ui/PlanMissions.client.tsx`); the plan it receives has the issue descriptions left out.
- Daily figures for the graphs and heat maps come from `domain/series.ts` (#1189): issues finished per day, the running total done and how many were open when each day ended, for the whole plan or any group of issues (a mission, a project). Days are the site's calendar, a quiet day is zero, and issues decided against are in none of them; an issue with no open date counts as open from before the first day (`createdAt`, read from GitHub with the rest of the issue).
- Activity over time and the order of missions come from one rule (`domain/activity.ts`, #1125). A mission's latest activity is the latest of an issue's close and its last change on GitHub (an edit, a comment, a label), across the mission's issues; the page uses this order only. Missions are ordered by it, most recent first; missions whose issues carry no date come last. A mission whose issues were only edited, not finished, still ranks by that edit. Activity is counted in weeks while at least half of the last 8 weeks are busy (3 or more finished issues across the plan), then in months over the last 6, then in years over the last 3; with no activity at all it stays on weeks.
- A mission (a milestone) has its own page: its name, how many of its issues are done with a progress bar, a quiet-or-not dot and its week as a heat map, then one box per project (an epic) that opens to its own week and its issues, all closed when the page loads. A project's box links to its own page, and each issue links to its page. An issue row shows its title with its state on the same line, and its number and close date below; labels are not shown on the rows. Titles drop the type prefix developers add ("feat:", "fix(ui):") and start with a capital (`domain/title.ts`). The page is static, refreshes with the plan, asks search engines not to index it and shows only what the plan shows; an unknown, malformed or unlisted mission number answers 404 (`ui/MissionPage.tsx`, #1129).
- Issue text is Markdown shown safely: raw HTML appears as text, only web links open (in a new tab), images show their description only, task lists read "Done" or "Not done", and no issue heading becomes the page's h1 (`ui/IssueMarkdown.tsx`).
- If GitHub can't be read at run time, the render fails, so the last good page stays. During `next build` the plan is empty and the page shows its empty state until the first visit.
- Without a token GitHub allows 60 reads an hour, which an hourly refresh of a larger plan can pass. Set `GITHUB_READ_TOKEN` (read-only) on the server. A wrong token makes GitHub answer 401 and the first render fail ([project facts](/docs/project.md)).
- Skipped pull requests: GitHub lists them with issues; the plan drops them.
